title: Provolone and Oregano Focaccia
changes_from_base: Part wholemeal and semolina dough, garlic oil instead of plain oil, and cubes of provolone with oregano on top.
summary: A nutty semolina and wholemeal focaccia brushed with garlic oil and studded with melting cubes of provolone and oregano.
equipment: cling film or a clean tea towel

steps.title: Garlic oil
steps.text: Warm the oil and sliced garlic over low heat 4-5 min, until the garlic is pale gold, then take off the heat. Strain and keep the oil and the garlic slices separately.

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Mix the white flour, wholemeal flour, semolina and yeast, then add the warm water and 1 tbsp of the garlic oil. Stir to a rough, sticky dough, rest 15 min and work in the salt. Semolina and wholemeal give a nutty, slightly golden crumb.

steps.title: Folds
steps.text: Fold every 30 min, four times, until the dough holds its shape a little and shows bubbles.

steps.title: Tin
steps.text: Brush the tin with 2 tbsp garlic oil, add the dough, turn it over and stretch it to the corners. Cover and leave about 1 h, until risen and puffy.

steps.title: Top
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220 °C (200 °C fan). Dimple the dough, press the provolone cubes and garlic slices into the hollows, sprinkle with oregano and drizzle with the last of the garlic oil.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 22-26 min, until golden and the cheese has melted into little browned pools; the centre reads about 96 °C. Cool 15 min before cutting into 12.

tips: Keep the garlic pale when infusing; browned garlic tastes bitter.
Cut the cheese in fairly large dice so it melts into pools rather than vanishing.
Fine semolina is best; coarse semolina makes a gritty crumb.
storage: Keep wrapped at room temperature for 1 day, then in the fridge for up to 3 days. Warm at 200 °C for 5 min; freeze for up to 1 month. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
